official_site.name: Georgia Secretary of State: My Voter Page (MVP)

model_plain: Most Georgians vote in person, either during three weeks of early voting (any early voting site in your county) or on Election Day at your assigned precinct. Anyone could also vote by mail, but requests closed October 23, and the drop boxes go away when early voting ends on October 30.

deadlines.rule: Online registration closed on Monday, October 5, 2026 (the fifth Monday before the election, O.C.G.A. 21-2-224). The Secretary of State's election page lists 'Last day to register to vote: October 5th.' If a December 1 runoff happens, the registration deadline depends on the race: for a runoff in a federal race (U.S. Senate or U.S. House) you can register through Monday, November 2, 2026; for a runoff in a state or local race the deadline stays October 5. Fulton County's official key dates list 'Voter Registration Deadline: Monday, October 5' and 'Voter Registration Deadline (Federal races): Monday, November 2' for the General Runoff, and Gordon County's 2026 election calendar shows the same two dates, with Nov. 2 marked 'Runoff for Federal Offices.'
Paper applications had to be postmarked by Monday, October 5, 2026 (VOTE411: 'online, mail (postmarked), and in-person registration' all closed that day).

In-person registration at a county registrar's office, a Georgia DDS (driver's license) office, or a public library closed Monday, October 5, 2026. Georgia has no same-day or Election Day registration.

registration.same_day_notes: None. Georgia does not allow registering and voting on the same day, during early voting or on Election Day. The only people who can still register for November 3 are military and overseas voters covered by federal UOCAVA rules.
registration.still_possible_now: Not for November 3. The deadline was Monday, October 5, 2026. If you think you registered, confirm it now at mvp.sos.ga.gov; if your record is wrong or missing, call your county elections office before you go vote. One exception worth knowing: if a federal race (U.S. Senate or U.S. House) goes to a December 1 runoff, you can still register to vote in that runoff through Monday, November 2 (Fulton County lists 'Voter Registration Deadline (Federal races): Monday, November 2'). For a runoff in a state or local race, the October 5 deadline still applies. If you moved within the same county after October 5, you can still vote (go to your old precinct, or update your address at the registrar's office and vote in the new one). If you moved to a different Georgia county within 30 days of the election (on or after October 4), vote in your old county. If you moved counties before that and didn't re-register there by October 5, call your county registrar; you may not be eligible this time (O.C.G.A. 21-2-218).

mail_ballot.who_gets_one: Nobody automatically. Any registered Georgia voter can vote by mail without giving a reason, but you must apply for each election. Counties began mailing ballots on Monday, October 5, 2026 (29 days before the election). Apply at the state's absentee portal (securemyabsenteeballot.sos.ga.gov), or send the paper form to your county by mail, email, fax or in person. The application must include your Georgia driver's license or state ID number; if you have neither, you attach a copy of another accepted ID. Voters 65 and older, voters with a disability, and military and overseas voters can file one application that covers the whole election cycle.

request_deadline.rule: Your county had to receive your application by Friday, October 23, 2026 (11 days before the election, O.C.G.A. 21-2-381). The SOS page says: 'First day to request an Absentee by Mail Ballot: August 17th (Last day is October 23rd).' That deadline has passed, so vote in person.

return_options: drop box, but only inside an early voting site, only during that site's early voting hours, and only through the last day of early voting (Friday, October 30). Georgia.gov: 'Drop boxes are available inside early voting locations, during early voting hours only.' Fulton: 'Last day to return the Absentee Ballot in the Drop Box: Friday, October 30.'
hand-deliver to your county board of registrars / elections office by 7:00 PM on Election Day (georgia.gov: 'take it to your County Board of Registrar's Office by 7 p.m. on Election Day')
mail (USPS), only if you allow at least a week; it 'must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day', postmarks don't count
a family member, someone who lives in your household, or your caregiver may deliver it for you; nobody else may (O.C.G.A. 21-2-385(a))
mail_ballot.postage: Not prepaid statewide. Most Georgia counties require you to put a First-Class stamp on the return envelope; a few provide prepaid envelopes. Follow the instructions printed on your envelope, or skip postage by using a drop box. Confidence: unverified for your county; check your envelope.
mail_ballot.signature_witness_rules: No witness, no notary, and since SB 202 there is no signature matching. Instead you sign the oath on the return envelope and write your Georgia driver's license or state ID number and your date of birth. If you have no Georgia license or ID, you write the last four digits of your Social Security number; if you have none of those, you enclose a copy of an accepted ID. Keep the inner privacy sleeve: a ballot returned without the sealed oath envelope can be rejected.
mail_ballot.cure_process: If your ID number or date of birth is missing or doesn't match, or the oath is unsigned, the county must notify you (by mail, and by phone or email if they have it) and your ballot is held as provisional. You fix it by returning a signed affidavit with a copy of an accepted ID. Georgia's cure window runs until the end of the third day after the election, Friday, November 6, 2026. SB 202 (O.C.G.A. 21-2-386) gives you 'until the end of the period for verifying provisional ballots,' and georgia.gov says provisional issues must be resolved 'within three days.' You can also check status on BallotTrax or My Voter Page.
mail_ballot.mail_cutoff_advice: Election officials and USPS say to mail at least 7 days before Election Day. In practice: if you still have your ballot after Monday, October 26, don't mail it. Put it in a drop box at an early voting site by close on Friday, October 30, or hand it to your county elections office by Tuesday, November 3 (call for hours: Fulton 404-612-7020, DeKalb 404-298-4020). If you decide to vote in person instead, bring the mail ballot with you so the poll manager can cancel it. If you never received it, you can still vote in person: georgia.gov says you'll 'sign a document attesting that you are only voting once.' Once you've returned your absentee ballot, you've voted and can't vote in person.

early_in_person.hours_note: Early voting (Georgia calls it 'advance voting') runs Tuesday, October 13 through Friday, October 30, 2026. The SOS page lists 'In Person Early/Advance Voting: October 13th - 30th' and georgia.gov says it 'ends on the Friday immediately prior to Election Day.' It started on a Tuesday because Monday, October 12 was a state holiday. Georgia.gov lists typical hours of 9 AM to 5 PM weekdays and 9 AM to 4 PM Saturdays, and says counties may go longer (many metro Atlanta sites run 7 AM to 7 PM). Required days are Monday through Friday plus 'the second and third Saturdays before Election Day,' which are October 17 and October 24, 2026 (georgia.gov has an event page for the first Saturday, October 17). Sunday voting (October 18 and 25) is optional by county; Fulton, DeKalb, Cobb and Gwinnett have offered it in recent elections. You can vote at any early voting site in your county. Exact sites and hours are on My Voter Page and your county elections site (Fulton announced 32 sites).

election_day.in_line_rule: Georgia.gov: 'As long as you are in line by 7 p.m., you are allowed to cast your ballot.' On Election Day you must vote at your assigned precinct (look it up on My Voter Page; it may differ from where you voted early). If you show up at the wrong precinct before 5:00 PM you'll be sent to the right one. After 5:00 PM you may cast a provisional ballot there only if you sign a statement that you can't get to your own precinct in time (SB 202, O.C.G.A. 21-2-418).

accepted: Georgia driver's license, even if expired
Georgia state ID card issued by DDS or a county registrar, including the free Georgia Voter Identification Card
Student ID from a Georgia public college or university (private-college IDs are not on the state's list)
Valid employee photo ID issued by any branch, department, agency or entity of the U.S. government, the State of Georgia, or any county, city or other Georgia government entity
A Georgia Voter ID card is free from any county registrar's office or DDS office if you have no other photo ID
id_rules.no_id_option: In person without photo ID: you can cast a provisional ballot, but it only counts if you bring an accepted ID to your county registrar's office within three days, by Friday, November 6, 2026 (georgia.gov: 'you must resolve eligibility issues with your County Registrar within three days'). By mail: no photo ID is needed if you write your Georgia driver's license or ID number and date of birth on the application and envelope; if you have no Georgia license or ID, use the last four of your Social Security number or enclose a copy of an accepted ID, or of a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check or other government document showing your name and address (Secretary of State voter ID page; VOTE411: 'Absentee applications require a Georgia driver's license or state ID number, or a copy of an accepted ID').

in_the_booth.phones_detail: Georgia law bars anyone from using a cell phone, camera, or other recording device inside the enclosed voting area of a polling place (O.C.G.A. 21-2-413(e)). Poll workers will tell you to put it away. Use your phone in line outside if you need to, then switch to paper once you check in. Source: SB 202 as enacted and the Georgia Code, https://www.legis.ga.gov/api/legislation/document/20212022/201498
in_the_booth.notes_detail: Yes. You can bring a printed sample ballot (print yours from My Voter Page), a handwritten list, or this guide on paper into the booth. Just don't show it to other voters or leave it behind: campaign material inside the polling place counts as electioneering. Source: Georgia Secretary of State voter guidance, https://georgia.gov/georgia-election-guide
in_the_booth.apparel_rule: No campaigning within 150 feet of the polling place building or within 25 feet of voters standing in line: no handing out literature, asking for votes, or displaying candidate or ballot-question gear. Poll managers can ask you to cover or remove a shirt, hat or button that names a candidate or issue on the ballot before you enter. Same statute (O.C.G.A. 21-2-414) bans giving voters in that zone anything of value, including food and water; see gotchas.

gotchas.text: Registration for November 3 is closed and there is no same-day registration. The deadline was Monday, October 5. One narrow exception: if a U.S. Senate or U.S. House race goes to a December 1 runoff, new voters can register for that runoff through Monday, November 2. A runoff for a state or local race keeps the October 5 deadline. Check that you're actually on the rolls at mvp.sos.ga.gov before you drive anywhere.
gotchas.short: Check that you're on the rolls at My Voter Page before you go.

gotchas.text: Drop boxes are not 24/7 and they vanish early. Since 2021 Georgia's boxes sit inside early voting sites, open only during those sites' voting hours, and they are pulled when early voting ends on Friday, October 30. After that, the only ways to return a mail ballot are to hand it to your county elections office (by 7:00 PM Nov. 3) or to mail it and hope it arrives in time. Postmarks do not count. If in doubt, vote in person and bring the mail ballot with you to cancel it.
gotchas.short: Drop boxes close Oct 30; after that, hand your ballot to your county office.

gotchas.text: Early voting is 'anywhere in your county.' Election Day is 'only your precinct.' From October 13 to 30 you can use any early voting site in your county. On November 3 you must go to your assigned precinct, which may be a different building. Look it up on My Voter Page the night before.
gotchas.short: Vote early anywhere in your county; on Election Day, only at your precinct.

gotchas.text: Don't hand out water or snacks to people in line. Under SB 202 it is a misdemeanor to give voters anything, including food and drink, within 150 feet of the polling place building. A federal judge blocked the extra '25 feet from any voter in line' part in 2023, but the 150-foot zone stands. Poll workers may set up self-serve water. If you expect a wait, bring your own water, a snack, and a paper cheat sheet (no phones inside).
gotchas.short: Don't hand out water or snacks within 150 feet; bring your own if you'll wait.

gotchas.text: Georgia makes you win a majority. If no candidate gets more than 50 percent, the top two meet in a runoff on Tuesday, December 1, 2026 (four weeks later). This year that is unlikely in the statewide races: the Libertarian Party failed to collect the roughly 70,000 signatures it needed, so every statewide race is a straight two-candidate contest (write-ins exist for Senate and governor but rarely move the number). If a runoff does happen anywhere, the early voting window is tiny: counties must offer it no later than Monday, November 23 through Wednesday, November 25 (georgia.gov: 'abbreviated due to the Thanksgiving holiday'), and some start sooner; Fulton lists Saturday, November 21 through Wednesday, November 25. Registration for a runoff stays open until November 2 only for federal races (U.S. Senate, U.S. House); state and local runoffs keep the October 5 deadline. If you vote by mail, you would need to apply again, by Friday, November 20 (Fulton and Gordon County calendars), unless you are 65+, disabled, or military/overseas.
gotchas.short: If no one tops 50 percent, the top two meet in a Dec 1 runoff.

situations.question: I moved to a new address in Georgia.
situations.short: Same county: vote at your old polling place this time; new county within 30 days: vote in your old county.
situations.answer: If you moved within the same county (say, within Fulton) and didn't update your registration in time, you can vote at your old polling place this time. If you moved to a different Georgia county within 30 days of the election, go back to your old county's precinct or vote early there.
steps: Still file your new address with your county registrar, online or on paper, so it's right next time.
Moved counties more than 30 days ago and didn't re-register by Oct 5? You can't vote in your old county, and it's too late to register in the new one. Call your county registrar if you're unsure.
Can't get back to your old county? Absentee requests closed Oct 23, so you'll need to vote in person there.

situations.question: I just moved to Georgia from another state.
situations.short: Georgia's deadline was Oct 5, so register now for future elections.
situations.answer: Georgia's registration deadline for November 3 was October 5, so if you weren't registered here by then, you can't vote in Georgia this time. Register now online so you're ready for future elections.
steps: Register at registertovote.sos.ga.gov.
If a U.S. Senate or U.S. House race goes to a December 1 runoff, new voters can register for that runoff through Monday, Nov 2.
Moved away from Georgia for good? You'd vote in your new state instead.

situations.question: I'm not registered to vote.
situations.short: The deadline was Oct 5, but check My Voter Page first, because you may be registered already.
situations.answer: We're sorry: Georgia's deadline was October 5 and there's no same-day registration, so you can't vote on November 3 if you missed it. First double-check on My Voter Page, because you may be registered already.
steps: Look yourself up at mvp.sos.ga.gov, or call your county registrar.
One exception: if a federal race goes to a December 1 runoff, you can register for that runoff through Monday, Nov 2.
Register now so you're set for the next election either way.

situations.question: The lookup can’t find me.
situations.short: The lookup needs your name exactly as registered: try your last name with the hyphen, a space, and joined.
situations.answer: Georgia’s My Voter Page asks for your first initial, last name, county and birth date, so a first-name spelling can’t be the problem. Try the last-name spellings below.
steps: Try your last name with the hyphen, with a space instead, and run together, and leave out any middle name or suffix.
Still nothing? Call your county election office. A failed search doesn’t mean you’re not registered; records can lag.

situations.question: I went to the wrong polling place.
situations.short: Early voting works at any site in your county through Oct 30; on Election Day, go to your precinct.
situations.answer: During early voting (through Friday, October 30), you can use any early voting site in your county. On Election Day you must vote at your assigned precinct; before 5 PM the poll workers will send you there.
steps: Look up your precinct on My Voter Page; it may be a different building from where you voted early.
After 5 PM, if you can't get to your own precinct in time, you can vote a provisional ballot where you are by signing a statement saying so.
In Fulton County, check your precinct the night before.

situations.question: My absentee ballot never came, or I lost it.
situations.short: Never arrived: cancel it in writing and vote in person; arrived then lost: call your county absentee office first.
situations.answer: If your absentee ballot never arrived, you may ask in writing to cancel it and sign a statement that you are voting only once. If it arrived and you then lost it, call your county absentee office before going to vote; we have not confirmed the received-then-lost procedure from an official source. Fulton County's absentee office is 404-612-7060. If you still have the ballot and want to vote in person, bring it to surrender to the poll manager.
steps: Check its status on My Voter Page (mvp.sos.ga.gov). Fulton: absentee office, 404-612-7060 or elections.absentee@fultoncountyga.gov. Other counties: your county registrar's office.
Vote early at any site in your county through Oct 30, or at your own precinct on Nov 3.

Received it but lost it? Call Fulton absentee voting at 404-612-7060, or your own county registrar, for replacement or cancellation instructions. Tell them whether the ballot was returned. If your completed ballot was already accepted, you cannot vote again.

situations.question: I made a mistake on my ballot.
situations.short: Absentee: bring it to the polls and hand it in; in person: tell a worker before you scan.
situations.answer: On an absentee ballot, bring it with you when you vote in person and hand it to the poll manager; then you vote a regular ballot. At the polls, check your printed ballot before you scan it, and if something's wrong, tell a poll worker before scanning.
steps: Absentee: take the ballot to an early voting site (through Oct 30) or your Election Day precinct.
In person: don't scan a ballot that's wrong. Ask for help first.

situations.question: I mailed my ballot but now want to vote in person.
situations.short: Once the county has it, you've voted; if you still have it, bring it to the polls and vote.
situations.answer: Once the county receives your absentee ballot, you have voted and can't change your mind. If you still have it, bring it to the polls and hand it to the poll manager, and you can vote a regular ballot.
steps: Check My Voter Page or BallotTrax to see whether it was received.
Mailed it but it hasn't arrived? You can ask in writing to cancel it and vote in person.

situations.question: I don't have an ID.
situations.short: Many IDs count, even an expired Georgia license; with none, get a free Voter ID card from your county registrar.
situations.answer: Georgia requires photo ID in person, but many count: a Georgia driver's license (even expired), a passport, a military or tribal ID, a government employee ID, or a student ID from a Georgia public college. If you have none, get a free Georgia Voter ID card at your county registrar's office or a Department of Driver Services office.
steps: No ID at the polls? You can vote a provisional ballot, then bring an accepted ID to your county registrar by Friday, Nov 6.
Voting absentee? You write your license or state ID number; if you have neither, you include a copy of an accepted ID or a document like a utility bill.

situations.question: My name changed since I registered.
situations.short: You can still vote: bring your photo ID, and update your name online for next time.
situations.answer: You can still vote. Bring your photo ID and update your registration with your new name online, so your record matches next time.
steps: Update your record at registertovote.sos.ga.gov (it lets you change an existing registration).
If poll workers can't confirm it's you, ask for a provisional ballot and settle it with your county registrar by Friday, Nov 6.

situations.question: I'm a college student.
situations.short: Vote where you're registered; absentee requests closed Oct 23, so vote in person in that county.
situations.answer: Registration closed October 5, so you vote where you're already registered. Absentee requests closed Friday, October 23. Already have your ballot? Use a drop box at an early voting site by Friday, Oct 30, or hand it to your county elections office by Nov 3 (call for hours: Fulton 404-612-7020, DeKalb 404-298-4020).
steps: Already have your ballot? Use a drop box at an early voting site by Friday, Oct 30, or hand it to your county elections office by Nov 3 (call for hours: Fulton 404-612-7020, DeKalb 404-298-4020).
A student ID from a Georgia public college (like Georgia State or Georgia Tech) counts as photo ID. Private-college IDs don't.
Registered at school in Fulton? Vote early at any Fulton site through Oct 30.

situations.question: I'll be away on Election Day.
situations.short: Vote early at any site in your county through Oct 30, or on Nov 3 at your own precinct.
situations.answer: Absentee requests closed Oct 23. You can still vote early in person through Friday, Oct 30 at any site in your county (Fulton or DeKalb), or on Nov 3 at your assigned precinct. Already have your mail ballot? Use a drop box at an early voting site by Friday, Oct 30, or hand it to your county elections office by Nov 3 (call for hours: Fulton 404-612-7020, DeKalb 404-298-4020).
steps: Drop boxes are inside early voting sites and close for good on Oct 30.
After that, hand it to your county elections office by Nov 3 (call for hours: Fulton 404-612-7020, DeKalb 404-298-4020).

situations.question: I'm in line when polls close.
situations.short: Stay in line: if you're in line by 7 PM, you can vote.
situations.answer: Stay in line. If you're in line by 7 PM, you're allowed to vote.
steps: Don't leave, even if the line is long.
Bring your own water and snacks; others can't hand them to you near the polls.

situations.question: They said there's a problem with my absentee ballot envelope.
situations.short: Return the signed cure form with an ID copy to your county registrar by Friday, Nov 6.
situations.answer: Georgia doesn't match signatures anymore; it checks your ID number, birth date and signed oath instead. If something's missing or doesn't match, your county will contact you, and you can fix it by returning a signed form with a copy of your ID by Friday, November 6.
steps: Watch your mail, email and phone after you return your ballot.
Return the cure form and ID copy to your county registrar right away.
Check My Voter Page or BallotTrax to confirm it was accepted.

situations.question: What's a provisional ballot?
situations.short: It's a paper ballot used when you can't be confirmed; it counts if the registrar confirms you within three days.
situations.answer: It's a paper ballot used when your eligibility can't be confirmed at the polls, like when your name isn't on the list or you don't have ID. It counts if your county registrar can confirm you're eligible within three days after Election Day.
steps: If it was about ID, bring an accepted photo ID to your county registrar by Friday, Nov 6.
Cast it in the county where you're registered.

situations.question: How do I check my ballot was counted?
situations.short: Check My Voter Page or sign up for BallotTrax; for a provisional ballot, ask your county registrar.
situations.answer: For an absentee ballot, log in to My Voter Page and look at Absentee Ballot Request Information, or sign up for BallotTrax alerts. For a provisional ballot, ask your county registrar.
steps: Log in at mvp.sos.ga.gov.
Or sign up at georgia.ballottrax.net.
If it shows a problem, fix it by Friday, Nov 6.

heads_up.text: If no candidate gets more than half the votes, the top two go to a Dec. 1 runoff.
